svg.text: Choosing the Migration Target Store — Warehouse vs Lakehouse SQL vs SQL Database vs Mirrored Source
A T-SQL-first, structured DW migration usually lands in Fabric Warehouse; the branches below say when it does not.
Migrating a data warehouse into Fabric —
which store should own the query surface?
Q1: Do you need writable, full T-SQL
(ACID DML, procs, views) on the target?
Yes — analytical T-SQL warehouse
Read-only T-SQL is enough
Transactional (OLTP) workload
FABRIC WAREHOUSE — default DW target
Pick when
• Enterprise star/snowflake marts, T-SQL-first team.
• Need multi-table ACID transactions, procs,
materialized views, COPY INTO / CTAS loads.
You get
• Tables stored as Delta on OneLake, no export.
• Polaris MPP + V-Order; serverless autoscale.
• Migration Assistant ports Synapse/SQL Server.
• Cross-DB T-SQL can join lakehouse + mirrored DBs.
Choose warehouse over lakehouse when Spark is not the primary tool.
LAKEHOUSE SQL ANALYTICS ENDPOINT
Pick when
• Spark is the primary tool, data is heterogeneous
/ largely unstructured; land raw then transform.
• T-SQL access needed only for reads / BI.
You get
• A read-only T-SQL endpoint auto-provisioned
over the lakehouse — same SQL engine as WH.
• No ACID DML surface — writes go through Spark.
Either store runs the same engine for T-SQL reads;
a warehouse can be added later if writes are needed.
SQL DATABASE IN FABRIC — OLTP
Pick when
• The workload is transactional (OLTP / translytical),
not an analytical warehouse.
• Same SQL Database Engine as Azure SQL Database.
You get
• A companion SQL analytics endpoint auto-created;
data auto-replicated to OneLake Delta for analytics.
• Entra-only auth; RLS/OLS; SqlPackage bacpac/dacpac
migration from Azure SQL Database.
Built on Hyperscale — compute/storage separated.
Q2 (orthogonal): Is the source an existing operational DB you want to keep as the system of record during migration?
FABRIC MIRRORING — the transitional bridge (use alongside any lane above)
When it fits
Data already in Azure SQL DB, Snowflake, Oracle,
Cosmos DB, BigQuery, SAP, SQL Server, etc.
Low-latency, low-cost replica into OneLake with
no source rebuild; ~15s propagation, free compute.
What it buys the migration
Lands Delta in OneLake — Direct Lake models and
cross-DB T-SQL work immediately, so you can run
Fabric BI in parallel while the source stays live,
then cut over to a Warehouse when ready.
Do NOT treat mirroring as the finish line if…
Source RLS/CLS/masking are dropped — rebuild security.
Not a backup / not a change stream; restart = full reseed.
SQL endpoint adds ~30–60s lag over the Delta layer.
Some connectors pause under Block Public Internet Access.
Anti-pattern — lift-and-shift that ignores the Delta/Polaris grain
• Porting trickle-DML ETL unchanged: each small INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE writes a new Parquet file → fragmented row groups, slow scans. Batch instead.
• Carrying over varchar(max) / unsized strings hurts statistics and cost estimation — size varchar(n) to the real data.
• Loading in tiny files: COPY INTO wants 100 MB–1 GB, many files for parallelism; a V-Order-off staging WH can feed a V-Order-on read WH.
Inference (Fabric Atlas, not a cited product fact):
These lanes are not mutually exclusive across a program — a common shape is Mirror the source for an early parallel run, then land a curated
Warehouse via Data Factory Copy and repoint the semantic models. The decision is per-workload, and the default for a T-SQL DW is the Warehouse.
All four targets read one OneLake Delta copy — the choice is query surface (writable T-SQL vs read-only vs OLTP vs live replica), not data duplication.
Fabric Atlas — original diagram, July 2026. Not a Microsoft asset.
